personal_inspection.affine: FakeQuantize explicitly states clamp(round(x/scale + zero_point), quant_min, quant_max), followed by subtracting zero_point and multiplying scale. Its zero_point definition is the quantized value corresponding to floating zero. Observer implementation first includes zero in min/max, uses range/(quant_max-quant_min), rounds the offset and clamps positive epsilon.
personal_inspection.math: There are 2^4=16 codes but 15 adjacent intervals. Exact rational width 3 divided by 15 is 1/5. For low=-1, zero=5; codes 0,5,10,15 decode to -1,0,1,2. For low=-2 and high=1, the width/scale is unchanged and zero=10.
personal_inspection.storage: The dtype table calls torch.uint8 unsigned 8-bit; the executed tensor has element_size 1, four elements and four bytes. No shift/OR packing exists in the original 17.4 fence.
personal_inspection.scope: This is a direct finite-value encoding/decoding demonstration. It performs no gradient computation, parameter update, training or model evaluation. Off-grid variants establish rounding loss; the original all-zero formula fails as explicitly disclosed. The repository helper supplies its own positive scale floor.
personal_inspection.packing: Repository pack_int4 adds 8 to signed integers -8..7, places even-indexed codes in low nibbles, and uses the same offset in unpack_int4. Signed zero corresponds to storage nibble 8. The 17.4 affine zero code is 5. Directly feeding its unsigned codes 10 and 15 to this packer is rejected, so the text's format warning is substantiated.
